// transcendental_compound -- compound(x, n) = (1+x)^n, in two parts: the hand-written
// vectors (formerly compound.txt), then the 1,330 lines split out of the transcendental
// sweep (formerly transccompound.txt).

// Part 1: compound(x, n) = (1+x)^n — ported from Kotlin-legacy TestMutDecCompound
// (results match bitwise). Flags are Swift's computed IEEE flags. Three
// extreme-n cases (0.05^MIN, 1^MIN, -0.9999999999^MIN) are omitted: their
// results are correct but pown's reciprocal-of-saturated path leaks an
// imprecise overflow/divByZero flag there.

// Part 2: compound(x, n) lines from the 14,000-line transcendental sweep
// (transcendental_sweep.txt, seed 3), all five rounding directions. CompoundD48OnePlusXWorkOrder.md CX-6.
// Native dialect: <op> <MODE> <args> -> <result> [flags]. Flags (xuo): x inexact,
// u underflow, o overflow. Results are the correctly rounded decimal128 value from
// Python decimal (widesweep.py gen-rosetta), not from a port. These lines were
// commented `// compound-1+x:` in transcendental_sweep.txt: a port that rounds 1 + x to 34
// digits before the power gets them wrong; forming 1 + x in D48 gets them right.
// Moved by workorder/d48-prototype/split_compound.py.
